results.title: HACK ATTACK — 8-Hour Inter-College Hackathon
results.details:
HACK ATTACK — 8-Hour Inter-College Hackathon

AMC Engineering College presents HACK ATTACK — an 8-Hour Inter-College Hackathon where students come together to build, collaborate, innovate, and create impactful technology solutions to real-world problems.

Participants will get the opportunity to work on problem statements revealed on the day of the hackathon and develop working prototypes within a limited time frame.

Event Details

  • Date: 15 October 2026
  • Reporting Time: 8:30 AM
  • Duration: 8 Hours
  • Venue: AMC Engineering College, Bengaluru
  • Event Type: Inter-College Hackathon
  • Participation: Open to students from all departments/specializations
  • Prize Pool: ₹20,000

Tracks

Participants can build solutions under any one of the following three tracks:

1. AI & ML

Build intelligent solutions that address real-world problems using Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Generative AI, Computer Vision, NLP, or related technologies.

2. Web & App Development

Create useful and impactful web or mobile applications that solve practical problems and improve user experiences.

3. Sustainability & Social Impact

Develop technology-driven solutions that contribute towards sustainability, accessibility, community welfare, or meaningful social impact.

Team Formation & Eligibility

  • The hackathon is open to college/university students.
  • Students from any academic specialization or department can participate.
  • Inter-college teams are allowed.
  • Inter-specialization/inter-department teams are allowed.
  • Teams can consist of 2–4 members.
  • A participant can be part of only one team.
  • Teams must register with accurate participant and college details.
  • All team members must carry a valid college/student ID for verification.

Problem Statements & Format

  • Problem statements will be revealed on the day of the hackathon.
  • Teams will select a problem statement aligned with one of the available tracks.
  • Participants will have 8 hours to ideate, develop, test, and present their solution.
  • The primary objective is to produce a working prototype/MVP that demonstrates the proposed solution.
  • Teams are expected to explain the problem, their approach, implementation, and impact during the final presentation/demo.
  • The number and details of problem statements will be announced at the beginning of the hackathon.

Hackathon Schedule

8:30 AM — Reporting & Registration Verification
Hackathon Briefing — Problem Statements & Guidelines Revealed
Development Phase — 8 Hours
Final Submission & Demo — At the end of the hackathon

The exact submission and presentation instructions will be communicated to participants during the event.

Rules

  1. Each team must consist of 2–4 participants.
  2. Participants must register through the official registration process.
  3. Participants can be part of only one team.
  4. Teams may use technologies, frameworks, libraries, APIs, and development tools relevant to their solution, subject to the hackathon guidelines.
  5. The solution should primarily be developed during the hackathon. Pre-existing libraries, frameworks, boilerplate code, and development tools may be used, but submitting an already-built project as the final solution is not permitted.
  6. Plagiarism or direct copying of another team's solution will result in disqualification.
  7. Teams must submit their project within the specified deadline.
  8. Teams must be able to demonstrate their working solution to the judging panel.
  9. Teams are responsible for bringing their own laptops and required development equipment.
  10. Participants must follow the instructions provided by the organizers and mentors throughout the event.
  11. Any form of misconduct, cheating, harassment, or disruption of the event may result in disqualification.
  12. The organizers reserve the right to disqualify teams that violate the rules or provide misleading information during registration.
  13. The decision of the judging panel and organizing committee will be final and binding.

Judging Criteria

Projects may be evaluated based on:

  • Innovation & Originality
  • Problem Understanding
  • Technical Implementation
  • Functionality & Working Prototype
  • Real-World Impact
  • Feasibility & Scalability
  • Presentation & Demonstration

What Participants Get

  • Opportunity to compete in an inter-college hackathon
  • ₹20,000 prize pool
  • Mentorship and guidance from industry experts
  • Networking with fellow developers and innovators
  • Opportunity to showcase technical and problem-solving skills
  • Certificates for participants
  • Prizes and goodies for winning teams

Title Sponsor

Connect2future — Unlock the Power of Connectivity

The event is supported by Connect2future, helping bring together students, technology, innovation, and real-world problem solving.

Important Note

  • Participants are requested to report by 8:30 AM on 15 October 2026 at AMC Engineering College, Bengaluru. Further instructions regarding problem statements, submissions, judging, and presentations will be provided at the venue.

  • Limited team slots available due to venue and event capacity.
  • Early-bird registrations are FREE for the first few teams.
  • Once the free early-bird slots are filled, registration may be subject to the applicable registration fee.

6-Hour Frontend Hackathon

One Problem. One Builder. Six Hours.

results.details:
CognitionNext '26

CognitionNext '26 is a two-round hackathon organized by Cognext AI in collaboration with Technovanza, VJTI, designed to bring together students passionate about Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.

Participants will get an opportunity to showcase their AI expertise, build innovative solutions, compete for a ₹1,00,000 prize pool, and potentially earn internship opportunities with Cognext AI.

Eligibility

  • Open to students form all Engineering Colleges.

  • Teams can consist of 1–2 participants.

  • Each participant can register with only one team.

  • Participants must complete Round 1 to qualify for Round 2.

Hackathon Theme

Artificial Intelligence 

Participants are encouraged to demonstrate their knowledge, projects, technical skills, and innovative applications of AI/ML.

Event Structure

Round 1 – Online Screening Round

Dates: 18th October 2026 – 21st October 2026
Mode: Online

Round 1 will be a screening round based on participants' work, achievements, and contributions in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.

Participants will be required to submit:

  • A summary highlighting their significant work, achievements, and contributions in AI/ML.

  • Their GitHub profile link.

  • Links to relevant projects, repositories, deployed applications, research work, or other proof of work.

Participants are strongly encouraged to provide project links, GitHub repositories, or other relevant evidence supporting their submissions.

The number of teams shortlisted for Round 2 will be announced by the organizers.

Round 2 – Offline Hackathon

Dates: 23rd October 2026 – 24th October 2026
Mode: Offline
Venue: Veermata Jijabai Technological Institute (VJTI), Mumbai
Duration: 12 hours

Shortlisted teams will participate in the offline hackathon and work on a problem statement based on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.

The problem statement, submission requirements, judging criteria, and weightages for Round 2 will be released by the organizers.

Participants will be required to develop and submit their solution within the specified deadline.

Prizes & Opportunities

Total Prize Pool worth: ₹1,00,000

Participants can compete for:

  • Prize Pool

  • Potential internship opportunities with Cognext AI

  • Certificates

  • Opportunity to showcase AI skills and projects

Internship details: To be announced by the organizers.

Rules & Guidelines

  1. Teams may consist of 1–2 participants.

  2. Each participant can register with only one team.

  3. Participants must complete Round 1 to qualify for Round 2.

  4. Round 1 submissions must include the required AI/ML work summary and GitHub profile.

  5. Round 2 teams must submit their final solution within the specified deadline.

  6. Plagiarism or submission of another participant's work may lead to disqualification.

  7. Participants must follow all instructions issued by the organizing team.

  8. AI tools are allowed in the Round 2, as per the guidelines provided by the organizers.

  9. Rules regarding the use of AI tools, APIs, open-source code, and previously developed work will be communicated by the organizers.

  10. The decision of the organizing and judging team will be final.

Registration Details

Registration Fee: Free

Registration Window: till 21st October 2026

Participant Limit: 1–2 members per team

Round 1: 18th October 2026 – 21st October 2026

Round 2: 23rd October 2026 – 24th October 2026

Important Dates

Event Date
Registration till 21st Oct 2026
Round 1 18th Oct 2026 – 21st Oct 2026
Round 2 23rd Oct – 24th Oct 2026
Prize Pool ₹1,00,000

Judging criteria and detailed Round 2 submission requirements will be released along with the problem statement.

Why Participate?

  • Showcase your AI/ML projects and technical achievements.

  • Compete in a 12-hour offline hackathon at VJTI.

  • Win from a ₹1,00,000 prize pool.

  • Get an opportunity to connect with Cognext AI.

  • Explore potential internship opportunities.

  • Earn certificates and gain valuable hackathon experience.

Whether you're passionate about AI/ML, Generative AI, Web & App Development, Cybersecurity, Blockchain, IoT, FinTech, or emerging technologies, this is your opportunity to build something impactful, learn from mentors, collaborate with fellow developers, and compete for a ₹1.5 Lakh prize pool.

Event Details

  • Event: 24 HR Hackathon
  • Fest: SPHINX'26
  • Date: 30 October 2026
  • Duration: 24 Hours
  • Start Time: 2:00 PM
  • Venue: VLTC, MNIT Jaipur
  • Prize Pool: ₹1,50,000

Eligibility

  • Open to college students and student developers from across India.

Team Size

Hackathon Format

The hackathon will be conducted as an intensive 24-hour build challenge.

Registration & Team Formation

Register individually or with your team and complete the required registration process.

Challenge Brief

Compete with multiple teams in an offline environment.

Participants can explore solutions across areas such as:

Rules

  • Inter-college and inter-specialization teams are permitted.
  • Teams must complete their project within the hackathon duration.
  • Participants must follow the official code of conduct and instructions provided by the organizers.
  • Teams must submit their project before the announced submission deadline.
  • Each team should be able to demonstrate and explain its project during evaluation.
  • Use of open-source libraries, APIs, frameworks, and publicly available tools is permitted, subject to the hackathon's guidelines.

Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters:

  • Innovation & Originality
  • Technical Implementation
  • Problem Relevance
  • Impact & Usefulness

What Participants Get

By participating in the hackathon, you get the opportunity to:

  • Build a real-world technology solution

Food & Accommodation

It's an opportunity to Take your idea from concept to a working prototype in 24 hours and experience the energy of one of Jaipur's major technology festivals.

results.title: Blitz'26 - Technical Coding
results.details:
Overview

Date: 13 October 2026
Venue: IT Lab

The coding event will consist of two compulsory rounds.

Round 1: Debugging

  • Duration: 45 minutes
  • Questions: 2 Easy, 1 Medium, 1 Hard
  • Participants will be given erroneous code and must identify and fix the errors.

Round 2: Coding

  • Duration: 60 minutes
  • Questions: 2 Easy, 1 Medium, 1 Hard
  • Participants must write their own code to solve the given problems.

Sample Questions

  • Sample questions will be shared with participants two days before the event.
  • Event questions may be based on the samples, with slight modifications. They will not be completely different from the provided samples.

Programming Languages: Participants may use Java, C, Go, or Python.

Test Cases

Each question will have five test cases:

  • 2 visible test cases
  • 3 hidden test cases

Evaluation Criteria

Participants will be evaluated based on:

  • Score obtained for each question.
  • Number of questions attempted.
  • Time taken to solve each question.

The best submission for each question will be considered for evaluation.

Rules and Restrictions

  • Both rounds are compulsory.
  • Each round has its own global timer.
  • The use of AI tools, internet access, and external assistance is strictly prohibited.

Give it your best, challenge yourself, and aim for the top. Good luck to everyone participating!

results.title: Threws Odyssey 2026
results.details:
Overview

THREWS ODYSSEY 2026 is an online research and innovation hackathon organised by Threws – The Research World.

The hackathon brings together students, developers, researchers and technology enthusiasts to build practical solutions to real-world problems across multiple domains.

Participants can choose a problem from one of the following tracks:

  • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
  • Medical & HealthTech
  • Cybersecurity
  • FinTech
  • ClimateTech & Sustainability
  • DeepTech & Scientific Computing
  • Smart Cities & Social Impact
  • Human-AI & Assistive Technology
  • Web3, Privacy & Decentralised Systems
  • Open Innovation

What to Build

Participants are expected to identify a meaningful problem and develop a working solution. Projects can be software products, AI/ML systems, research prototypes, cybersecurity solutions, data-driven applications or other technology-based solutions relevant to the selected track.

Projects should demonstrate a clear problem statement, a well-defined approach and a functional prototype. Participants are encouraged to research existing solutions and explain how their approach improves upon or differs from them.

Eligibility

  • Open to college students, freshers, professionals, researchers and independent developers.
  • Participants from any academic or technical background can apply.
  • Participation is open to individuals as well as teams.
  • Maximum team size: 2 members.
  • Participants may choose any one of the available tracks.

Hackathon Process

  • Register for THREWS ODYSSEY 2026.
  • Select a track and identify a problem.
  • Develop the solution during the hackathon period.
  • Test and refine the project.
  • Submit the project before the submission deadline.
  • Submissions will be reviewed by the judging panel.
  • Shortlisted participants may be invited for a final demonstration or presentation.
  • Winners will be announced after the final evaluation.

Submission Requirements

Each submission must include:

  • Project name
  • Problem statement
  • Description of the proposed solution
  • Key features
  • Technology stack
  • Source code / repository
  • Working prototype or demonstration
  • Brief explanation of the implementation
  • Dataset and external resources used, where applicable
  • Results or evaluation, where applicable

A short demo video may also be requested for shortlisted projects.

Judging

Projects will be evaluated on:

  • Innovation and originality
  • Technical implementation
  • Relevance and importance of the problem
  • Quality of the solution
  • Research, experimentation and use of data where applicable
  • Potential impact and scalability
  • Quality of the final demonstration

Rules

  • Submissions must be the original work of the participating individual or team.
  • Pre-existing projects may be used as a starting point only if substantial new work is carried out during the hackathon and clearly disclosed.
  • Participants may use open-source libraries, APIs, datasets and development tools, subject to their respective licences.
  • Use of AI coding and research tools is permitted. Participants must understand the work submitted under their name and be able to explain it during evaluation.
  • All third-party resources must be properly acknowledged.
  • Plagiarism, copied submissions, fabricated results or misrepresentation of work may result in disqualification.
  • Each participant may be part of only one team.
  • Projects must comply with applicable laws, licences and ethical standards.
  • The organisers reserve the right to reject submissions that do not meet the eligibility or submission requirements.
  • The decision of the judging panel will be final.

The objective of THREWS ODYSSEY is simple: find meaningful problems, explore better solutions and build something that can make a difference.

Build something worth discovering.

Prizes & Recognition

Total Prize Pool: ₹1,50,000

results.details:
NexHack 3.0 — Build What's Next

48 Hours. Limitless Ideas. Real-World Impact.

Welcome to NexHack 3.0, an online hackathon organized by NexHack to bring together student developers, designers, problem-solvers, and innovators from across India.

This is your opportunity to turn an idea into a working project, collaborate with talented people, experiment with new technologies, and showcase your creativity.

Whether you're an experienced developer or participating in your first hackathon, NexHack invites you to learn, build, experiment, and innovate.

Event Overview

  • Event: NexHack 3.0
  • Organizer: NexHack
  • Mode: Online
  • Dates: 1–3 November 2026
  • Hackathon Duration: 48 hours
  • Registration Fee: Free
  • Team Size: 1–4 members
  • Eligibility: Students from colleges and universities
  • Prize Pool: ₹25,000
  • Certificates: Every eligible participant will receive a digital certificate, subject to the event's participation and submission requirements.

The exact 48-hour start time, submission deadline, and final presentation schedule will be announced through our official channels.

Theme: Build for a Better Tomorrow

Build technology that solves meaningful problems. Choose a track that interests your team and develop an innovative, practical solution.

1. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

  • Build intelligent applications that improve productivity, automate tasks, support decision-making, or solve real-world problems using AI and machine learning.
  • Example ideas: AI study assistant, document summarizer, intelligent accessibility tool, or workflow automation.

2. Education and Student Innovation

  • Use technology to make learning more accessible, personalized, and effective.
  • Example ideas: peer-learning platforms, study planners, skill-development tools, or student collaboration systems.

3. Sustainability and Environment

  • Develop solutions for environmental awareness, waste reduction, resource management, and sustainable communities.
  • Example ideas: waste segregation assistant, energy monitoring dashboard, or campus sustainability tracker.

4. Smart Society and Social Impact

  • Solve everyday problems faced by communities through accessible and useful technology.
  • Example ideas: local issue reporting, public transport information, accessibility solutions, or community resource platforms.

5. Open Innovation

  • Have an idea that doesn't fit the other tracks? Build something original that solves a clearly defined problem and demonstrates meaningful value.
  • Teams may use relevant technologies such as web development, mobile development, AI and machine learning, cloud computing, APIs, and open-source tools.

These are suggested tracks and example ideas, not mandatory problem statements. Final track rules will be shared by the organizers.

Prize Pool — ₹25,000

  • First Place: ₹12,000
  • Second Place: ₹8,000
  • Third Place: ₹5,000
  • Total Prize Pool: ₹25,000
  • Prize distribution is subject to the final event rules and confirmed funding. Any additional rewards, sponsor credits, or special awards will be announced officially.

Who Can Participate?

  • Students from colleges and universities.
  • Solo participants and teams of up to four members.
  • Beginners and experienced builders alike.
  • Participants interested in coding, design, AI, product development, and innovation.

Cross-college and interdisciplinary teams are welcome, subject to the final registration rules.

How It Works

  • Step 1 — Register: Complete the free registration process.
  • Step 2 — Form Your Team: Participate solo or create a team of 2–4 members.
  • Step 3 — Build: Develop a project during the official 48-hour hackathon period.
  • Step 4 — Submit: Share your project repository, description, and demo before the deadline.
  • Step 5 — Get Evaluated: Judges assess submissions using the published scoring criteria.
  • Step 6 — Winners Announced: Final results will be shared through official NexHack channels.

Project Submission Requirements

Each team must submit:

  • Project name and selected track.
  • Problem statement and proposed solution.
  • Project description and key features.
  • GitHub repository or equivalent source-code link.
  • README with setup instructions and technology stack.
  • Demo video or working demo link.
  • Brief explanation of each team member's contribution.

Projects must comply with the final submission guidelines and deadline announced by the organizers.

Judging Criteria

Projects will be evaluated out of 100 points:

  • Innovation and Originality — 20 points
  • Problem Relevance — 20 points
  • Technical Implementation — 25 points
  • Potential Impact — 20 points
  • Presentation and Demo — 15 points

The judges' decisions will be final. Tie-breaking rules and the final judging process will be published in the official guidelines.

Rules and Guidelines

  • Each participant may register for only one team.
  • Teams must follow the announced team-size and eligibility requirements.
  • Projects must be original and comply with the event's development rules.
  • Existing libraries, APIs, frameworks, and permitted open-source components may be used, with appropriate attribution.
  • AI tools may be used, but significant AI assistance and third-party components should be disclosed where required.
  • Plagiarism, fraudulent submissions, harassment, or misrepresentation may result in disqualification.
  • Teams must submit all required materials before the official deadline.
  • Participants must follow the organizers' code of conduct and final event guidelines.
  • Prize eligibility and certificate requirements will be determined by the published rules.

Certificates and Recognition

  • Eligible participants will receive digital participation certificates in accordance with the announced requirements. Winning teams will receive winner recognition, and finalist or special-award certificates may be offered if announced by the organizers.

Sponsors and Partners

  • We appreciate the organizations supporting student innovation and technology.

Potential or announced partners:

  • CollegeCrave — https://www.collegecrave.in/
  • ASAPTool — https://www.asaptools.in/

Sponsor names, logos, and benefits will be displayed in accordance with confirmed partnerships.

Round 1: Online GitHub & Portfolio Screening

Teams will be evaluated on their previous work, technical skills, individual contributions, and problem-solving ability.
The Team Leader must provide the required links and details for every team member. The top 60 teams will qualify for the offline hackathon.

results.title: ChronoForge
results.details:
About the Hackathon

ChronoForge is a 24-hour hackathon that brings together aspiring developers, creative thinkers, and technology enthusiasts to design and build innovative solutions to real-world problems. The event encourages participants to experiment with emerging technologies, push the boundaries of conventional problem-solving, and transform their ideas into functional prototypes.

Whether you're passionate about artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, cybersecurity, or software development, ChronoForge is an opportunity to put your skills to the test, collaborate with like-minded individuals, and turn ambitious ideas into practical solutions.

Participants will submit proposals aligned with the hackathon theme and their chosen track. The strongest proposals will be shortlisted for the hacking round, where teams will develop, refine, and demonstrate their solutions.

With dedicated tracks for Agentic AI and Cybersecurity, ChronoForge aims to encourage innovation across two exciting areas of technology.

Total Prize Pool: ₹50,000

Tracks

Agentic AI

Build intelligent systems that go beyond generating responses to autonomously reason, plan, use tools, and execute tasks. Explore how AI agents can solve complex problems, automate workflows, and enable new forms of human-machine collaboration.

Potential Areas Include

  • Autonomous AI agents for real-world problem-solving.
  • Multi-agent systems and collaborative intelligence.
  • AI-powered workflow automation and productivity tools.
  • Tool-using agents that interact with APIs, databases, and external systems.
  • Research assistants, personal assistants, and intelligent task managers.
  • Domain-specific agents for education, healthcare, finance, and other applications.
  • AI systems capable of planning, decision-making, and adaptive problem-solving.
  • Responsible, reliable, and human-centered agentic applications.

Participants are encouraged to develop solutions that demonstrate meaningful autonomy, effective tool usage, and measurable value beyond a conventional chatbot.

Cybersecurity

Develop innovative solutions that strengthen digital security, protect user privacy, and address emerging cyber threats. Explore how technology can help identify vulnerabilities, detect suspicious activity, improve digital trust, and make systems more resilient.

Potential Areas Include

  • AI-assisted threat detection and security analysis.
  • Network traffic analysis and anomaly detection.
  • Phishing, scam, and malicious URL detection.
  • Privacy-preserving applications and secure authentication.
  • Security monitoring and incident analysis tools.
  • IoT and connected-device security.
  • Vulnerability assessment and defensive security automation.
  • Security awareness, digital identity, and data protection.
  • Threat intelligence and security tools for developers.

Participants are encouraged to build practical, responsible security solutions that demonstrate clear technical value. Projects must operate within authorized environments and comply with applicable laws and ethical guidelines.

Eligibility

  • ChronoForge is open to students interested in technology, software development, and innovation.
  • Students from any academic specialization or discipline are welcome to participate.
  • Participants from different colleges and universities may form teams, subject to the event's team formation guidelines.
  • NITK Surathkal students will participate in the hackathon offline at NITK Surathkal.
  • Participants who are not NITK students will participate online.
  • All participants must provide accurate information during registration.
  • Each participant may be part of only one team.

Team Formation

  • Participants must register as teams of 2-4 members.
  • Teams may comprise students from different academic years and specializations.
  • Each team must designate one member as its team leader for registration, communication, and submission purposes.
  • Teams must select one primary track: Agentic AI or Cybersecurity.
  • The track chosen during the proposal stage will continue in throughout the hackathon and cannot be changed.

Hackathon Format and Process

ChronoForge will consist of a proposal screening round followed by a 24-hour hacking round for shortlisted teams.

Round 1: Proposal Submission and Screening

Teams must submit a project proposal aligned with their chosen track. The proposal should clearly communicate the problem being addressed, the proposed solution, its intended users, and its potential impact. Teams are encouraged to demonstrate originality, technical feasibility, and a clear implementation plan.

The screening submission should include

  • Problem statement and motivation.
  • Selected track: Agentic AI or Cybersecurity.
  • Proposed solution and key features.
  • Target users and intended use cases.
  • Proposed technology stack.
  • Innovation and differentiation from existing solutions.
  • Feasibility and implementation plan.
  • Expected impact and potential for scalability.
  • Prototype, wireframes, demo, or GitHub repository, if available.

Selection Process

The top 30 teams with the strongest proposals will advance to the hacking round.

Proposals will be evaluated based on originality, relevance to the selected track, feasibility, technical depth, and potential impact.

Round 2: The 24-Hour Hacking Round

The shortlisted teams will participate in the 24-hour hacking round, where they will turn their proposals into working prototypes.

Participation Format

  • NITK Surathkal students will participate offline at NITK Surathkal.
  • Participants from other institutions will participate online.
  • Teams are expected to develop and demonstrate the core functionality of their proposed solutions within the allotted time.

During the Hacking Round, Teams Will Be Expected To

  • Build a functional prototype or proof of concept.
  • Implement the core features of their proposed solution.
  • Demonstrate the technical approach and appropriate use of technology.
  • Document the implementation, architecture, and technology stack.
  • Explain the problem, solution, and intended impact.
  • Submit the final project within the communicated deadline.

Further details regarding the schedule, venue, online participation procedure, final submission requirements, and judging format will be communicated through the official event channels.

Prizes and Recognition

ChronoForge features a total prize pool of ₹50,000, with recognition for outstanding projects at both the overall and track levels.

Overall Awards

  • Overall Winner
  • Overall Runner-up

Track-wise Awards

  • Agentic AI — Track Winner
  • Agentic AI — Track Runner-up
  • Cybersecurity — Track Winner
  • Cybersecurity — Track Runner-up

Certificates

  • Participation certificates will be provided to all eligible participants.
  • Merit certificates will be awarded to the winners and runner-ups.

Prize allocation among the award categories and any additional rewards will be communicated by the organizers.

Evaluation Criteria

Projects will be evaluated by the judging panel based on the following criteria:

  • Problem Relevance: Clarity, importance, and significance of the problem being addressed.
  • Innovation: Originality, creativity, and differentiation from existing solutions.
  • Technical Implementation: Quality of implementation, technical depth, and effective use of the chosen technologies.
  • Functionality: Completeness of the prototype and demonstration of its core features.
  • Impact and Practicality: Potential to address real-world needs and deliver meaningful value.
  • Scalability: Potential for the solution to evolve and serve a broader set of users.
  • User Experience: Usability, accessibility, and quality of the overall experience.
  • Track Alignment: Relevance to the selected track and effective application of its underlying concepts.

For Agentic AI projects, judges may additionally consider meaningful autonomy, tool integration, planning, reliability, and outcome verification.

For Cybersecurity projects, judges may additionally consider the quality of threat analysis, effectiveness of defensive measures, technical rigor, and responsible implementation.

Rules and Guidelines

  • All project proposals and final submissions must be the original work of the participating team.
  • Each team must select one primary track for its submission.
  • Teams are expected to build their final projects during the allotted hacking period, based on the proposal submitted during screening.
  • Participants may use open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, models, and publicly available datasets, subject to their applicable licenses and terms of service.
  • Third-party assets, code, datasets, and models must be appropriately acknowledged.
  • Previously developed projects may not be submitted as new work without substantial development during the hackathon.
  • Plagiarism, unauthorized copying, impersonation, and misrepresentation of contributions are prohibited.
  • Teams must comply with applicable laws, ethical standards, and platform policies.
  • Cybersecurity projects must be developed and demonstrated only in authorized environments. Unauthorized access, testing against third-party systems, or malicious activity is strictly prohibited.
  • AI-based projects should be developed responsibly, with appropriate consideration for privacy, security, reliability, and potential misuse.
  • Teams must submit their final projects within the deadline announced by the organizers. Late submissions may not be considered.
  • Teams must be prepared to demonstrate their solutions and explain their technical implementation to the judges.
  • Participants attending offline must follow all venue and event-management instructions.
  • Online participants must comply with the submission, communication, and participation procedures specified by the organizers.
  • The organizers reserve the right to disqualify teams that violate the rules or provide misleading information.
  • The decisions of the judging panel regarding rankings and awards will be final.
  • Any changes to the schedule, rules, prizes, or participation requirements will be communicated through the official event channels.

Important Information

  • Hackathon: ChronoForge
  • Format: 24-hour hackathon
  • Total Prize Pool: ₹50,000
  • Tracks: Agentic AI and Cybersecurity
  • Selection Process: Proposal screening followed by the hacking round
  • Shortlisted Teams: Top 30 teams
  • NITK Students: Offline participation at NITK Surathkal
  • Non-NITK Participants: Online participation
  • Awards: Overall Winner, Overall Runner-up, Track-wise Winners and Runner-ups
  • Certificates: Participation certificates for all eligible participants; merit certificates for winners and runner-ups

Participants are advised to regularly check the official Unstop listing and the organizers' communication channels for announcements, deadlines, participation instructions, and other updates.

Welcome to D3COY: Outsmart the Obvious!

D3COY is a 24-hour national-level innovation hackathon organized by the DJSISACA Student Chapter at DJSCE. This event brings together developers, designers, problem-solvers, and tech enthusiasts to tackle real-world challenges in security, privacy, and digital trust.The hackathon challenges participants to strip away the safety nets, think beyond conventional solutions, and develop resilient, technically sound products within a high-intensity 24-hour adversarial environment. You will not only build but also adapt in real-time to unscripted mid-event curveballs and live constraints.Participants will have the opportunity to showcase their technical skills, adaptability, creativity, and problem-solving abilities while competing with top teams from across partner colleges, all while being judged and mentored by industry professionals.

Round 0 - PPT Screening (Selection Round) : 

The journey to D3COY begins with our online screening round. All teams will be provided with a single, common Problem Statement (PS) for Round 0. You will be evaluated based on your unique approach to solving this specific challenge.

Selection will be based on:

  •   Quality and originality of the proposed solution (PPT submission based on the provided common Problem Statement).
  •   Technical understanding of the problem statement.
  •   Feasibility and potential impact of the proposed approach.
  •   Unique Selling Proposition (USP) and Future Scope, demonstrating what sets

    your idea apart and how it can be scaled or applied in the real world.

Teams must submit their solution PPT and the resumes of all team members as part of the Round 0 submission. The top 36 shortlisted teams will earn the exclusive opportunity to advance to the on-site 24-hour hackathon at the DJSCE campus.

Team Formation : 

  •   Team Size: Minimum 2 and Maximum 4 members per team.
  •   Inter-College Teams: Allowed (Team members can be from different colleges).

Registration Fee :

Registration Fee: ₹200 per team. (Note: This entry fee applies only to the Round 0 selection phase. Teams that are shortlisted will not have to pay any additional fees for the main 24-hour offline hackathon).

Accommodation, Meals & Perks (For Shortlisted Teams) : 

  •   On-campus workspace and accommodation will be provided strictly for the 24-hour duration of the offline hackathon.
  •   Please note: No accommodation will be provided prior to the start of the event or after the event concludes.
  •   The 24-hour on-campus stay includes full meals, refreshments, and exclusive sponsor goodies/swag for all 

Who Can Participate  (For the Main 24-Hour Hackathon)

D3COY is open to all undergraduate students from any branch or background. Whether you are a security enthusiast, an AI developer, or a general innovator, there is a track for you. For the final on-site hackathon, participants will build solutions in one of the following tracks:

  •   Network & Infrastructure Security: Build tools that defend shared,high-traffic systems from intrusion or abuse.

About the Hackathon

Ecclesia 2026 Hackathon is a technology and innovation competition that challenges undergraduate students to identify real-world problems and develop innovative, practical, and technology-driven solutions. Eligibility and Team Formation

  4. Teams must prepare and submit a PowerPoint presentation explaining their proposed solution.

An alert just fired. Checkout is failing. Can your team find out why before the clock runs out?

KEEP ALIVE '26 is a national incident response championship for students who have been learning DevOps. You've practised Linux, Docker and Kubernetes. Now test it on the field: read the alerts, dashboards, logs and traces of a live microservices system, find what broke and why, and explain how you would fix it.

It runs on the same incident platform as Panic at the Pod, the live Kubernetes incident challenge by CNCG Noida, our Community Partner. KEEP ALIVE takes that format nationwide, built and scaled for students. It is hosted by GDG on Campus IIIT Nagpur at TantraFiesta 2026, the national technical fest of IIIT Nagpur.

Why take part

  • ₹25,000 in cash prizes for the top three teams and the Sharpest RCA award
  • Investigate real incidents on a real observability stack: Grafana dashboards, Prometheus metrics, logs and traces
  • No production experience needed. A 30-minute hands-on session at the finale teaches every tool you will use
  • After the finale, the platform team walks everyone through all 10 incidents and how they were solved
  • Goodies and certificates for every finalist, and merit certificates for the winners
  • Bring your senior: one recent graduate (2024 to 2026) of your college can join your team

Round 1: The Night Shift (online, 11 to 18 October)

  • One 30-minute assessment per team, taken once from the team leader's account
  • Multiple-choice questions on DevOps and observability, one incident to investigate from screenshots of dashboards, logs and traces, and two short written answers
  • Proctored and taken in full screen. No AI tools, no search and no second device
  • The top 15 teams reach the finale. The next 10 teams form the waitlist

Finale: KEEP ALIVE Live (on campus, 26 October, IIIT Nagpur)

  • A hands-on session on the platform, Grafana and the report form, with one practice incident
  • Phase 1, First Responder: 6 incidents in 90 minutes
  • Phase 2, Deep Dive: 3 intermediate incidents and 1 critical, cascading incident in 90 minutes
  • You never change the system. You read its signals and submit a short solution report for each incident: the root cause, the evidence and the fix
  • Each team presents its findings to the judges in a 10-minute slot

Who can join

  • Teams of exactly 3, all from the same college
  • UG, PG and diploma students from any branch or year
  • Up to one alumnus per team, graduated in 2024, 2025 or 2026. Working alumni are welcome
  • PhD students and research scholars are not eligible
  • Made for students with atleast 6 to 12 months of DevOps learning: if you have used Linux and Docker, run kubectl and opened Grafana a few times, you are ready

  • Round 1 window: Sunday, 11 October, 9:00 AM to Sunday, 18 October, 11:59 PM
  • Finalists and waitlist announced: Monday, 19 October, 6:00 AM

Good to know

  • Travel and stay for the finale are arranged by each team. Every team brings at least 2 laptops
  • AI tools, search and documentation are allowed in the finale, but every team must be able to explain what it submits
